differential.name: Insulin‑induced hypoglycemia
differential.rationale: Low fasting glucose (68 mg/dL) in a diabetic on dialysis suggests excess insulin or sulfonylurea effect, common in CKD with reduced drug clearance.

differential.name: Renal failure‑associated hypoglycemia
differential.rationale: Advanced CKD (stage 4) impairs insulin degradation, predisposing to spontaneous hypoglycemia even without overt overdose.

differential.name: Secondary adrenal insufficiency
differential.rationale: Chronic illness and possible glucocorticoid withdrawal can blunt cortisol response, leading to low glucose levels.

differential.name: Septicemia (early sepsis)
differential.rationale: Infection in a dialysis patient can present with hypoglycemia before overt fever or leukocytosis.

differential.name: Protein‑energy malnutrition
differential.rationale: Limited social contact and chronic illness may cause inadequate intake, contributing to low glucose readings.
